useful_delta: Evidence-backed candidate architecture for a generic worker execution fabric that preserves Prometeo's prepared JOB -> independent Run -> durable RETURN model while adding explicit allocation leases, missed-launch proof, bounded stale detection, deterministic retry/supersession, idempotent side-effect receipts, transport reconciliation and falsification tests. It does not invent a central mutable scheduler or treat transport acknowledgements as execution truth.

generic_run_allocation_model.principle: Separate logical work intent, dispatch attempts, execution ownership and result evidence. Durable source facts are authoritative; queue/running counts are derived views.
generic_run_allocation_model.logical_identity: A prepared Work Item remains the stable logical unit. A dispatch_id identifies one launch intent for that Work Item/generation. A worker_instance_id identifies one actual execution attempt and is never silently reused for a semantically different attempt.
allocation_flow: 1. Planner/Controller publishes a prepared JOB before any worker exists.
2. Executor derives a stable dispatch_id from parent/work-item/execution-generation and records or can reconstruct the requested launch intent.
3. Capacity admission chooses an execution slot only when bounded runner capacity is available; excess ready work remains QUEUED rather than disappearing.
4. Slot ownership is a lease/claim with owner, lease_epoch, acquired_at and expires_at. Claim creation/update uses compare-and-swap or equivalent create-if-absent semantics.
5. Worker creates its independent run artifact before substantive execution. Observation of that durable artifact, not a chat/API ACK, proves launch.
6. Worker writes only its declared scope. Aggregate parent/batch state is compiled from JOB/run/RETURN/consumption facts; workers never increment a shared counter.
7. RETURN is durable completion evidence; later integration/consumption remains a separate parent/steward act.
generic_run_allocation_model.capacity_rule: Capacity is a configurable runner profile, not a universal Prometeo constant. The controller may expose M ready jobs while each execution backend admits only its current safe bounded capacity. No historical chat-count observation may become a hard-coded global limit.
generic_run_allocation_model.anti_bottleneck_rule: Do not use one globally rewritten scheduler/status document. Prefer independent intent/run/claim facts and derived projections so unrelated allocations do not serialize on a central mutable file.

source_lifecycle: CREATED -> QUEUED -> STARTED -> WORKING -> RETURNED -> INTEGRATED
Current control-plane practice may render a fully returned scoped worker as DONE; derived normalization should map that without requiring duplicate worker state.
derived_liveness_overlay: REQUESTED_NO_ARTIFACT: dispatch intent exists but no run artifact has been observed yet.
LIVE: lease valid and recent durable progress/heartbeat/probe evidence exists.
SUSPECT: expected progress evidence is late but the lease has not yet been conclusively revoked.
STALE_RECOVERABLE: lease expired or probe/reconciliation proves the attempt no longer owns execution rights.
ZOMBIE: an old/superseded worker reappears after ownership moved; it is observable but must not regain write authority.
RETURN_AVAILABLE: durable RETURN exists regardless of whether callback/notification was delivered.

required_parameters: heartbeat_or_progress_interval when the backend supports it
timeout_profile.rule: Numeric defaults belong to measured runner profiles/canaries, not this architecture scout. lease_ttl must be comfortably greater than expected progress cadence and tolerate publication/transport jitter.
timeout_profile.clock_rule: Prefer service/repository timestamps or monotonic runner clocks for lease calculations. Treat cross-host wall-clock time as evidence with skew tolerance, not absolute truth.

worker_state_machine_and_timeouts.stale_transition_rule: Use at least two pieces of evidence before replacement when possible: silence/deadline plus expired ownership lease or failed backend reconciliation. Transport disconnect alone does not prove worker death.
worker_state_machine_and_timeouts.write_revocation_rule: Once a lease is revoked/superseded, the predecessor may not perform canonical/shared side effects. Late diagnostic RETURN data may be retained only in its isolated run namespace if allowed by its scope.

retry_and_supersession_rules.launch_retry: If dispatch was requested but no run artifact is observed by launch_ack_deadline, retry the same logical dispatch_id. Create-if-absent/idempotency guards ensure an ACK-loss retry cannot create a second logical launch accidentally.
retry_and_supersession_rules.execution_retry: Create a new worker_instance_id only after the earlier attempt is proven non-owning (terminal, lease revoked, or explicitly superseded) or after a policy-authorized timeout. The new run links supersedes=<old id>; the old run links superseded_by=<new id> when its owner/steward can safely record that fact.
retry_and_supersession_rules.no_identity_reuse: Never reset a stale run back to STARTED to represent a different attempt. New execution means new run identity with lineage.
retry_and_supersession_rules.winner_rule: Execution ownership is determined by the current valid lease/supersession generation, not by which chat answers last. A predecessor that returns after supersession cannot reclaim canonical write rights.
retry_and_supersession_rules.retry_budget: Use bounded exponential backoff with jitter and a per-profile/per-job attempt budget. Exhaustion produces durable BLOCKED/FAILED evidence for the parent rather than infinite retry loops.
retry_and_supersession_rules.replan_rule: If retry requires a materially changed mission, scope, authority baseline or return contract, it is no longer merely another run of the same Work Item; the Planner/Controller should publish a revised/new Work Item with lineage.
retry_and_supersession_rules.integration_rule: Retry/supersession chooses execution ownership only. It does not auto-promote a RETURN into Current/Human Accepted/Served.

missed_launch_detection.proof_rule: Requested launch and observed launch are separate facts. A durable run artifact is the minimum cross-transport proof that the worker actually started; API/chat submit ACKs are delivery telemetry only.
missed_launch_detection.detector: A reconciler compares expected dispatch intents/prepared jobs against repository-visible runs. If a dispatch has no matching run by launch_ack_deadline, emit MISSED_LAUNCH/REQUESTED_NO_ARTIFACT and keep unrelated ready work moving.
missed_launch_detection.ack_loss_case: If submit succeeded but the ACK was lost, the retry uses the same dispatch_id and first checks for the run artifact before creating another attempt.
missed_launch_detection.silent_drop_case: If transport accepted/requested work but no run artifact ever appears, retry through the same or an alternate permitted adapter after bounded backoff; do not describe the worker as active.
missed_launch_detection.incident_anchor: INC-ZM-BOOT-01 already demonstrated the exact unsafe ambiguity: dispatch was attempted, but no GitHub-visible run/return existed. Therefore 'requested' or 'sent' must never be rendered as started without artifact proof.

idempotency_keys.dispatch: stable dispatch_id per logical launch intent
idempotency_keys.external_side_effect: stable side_effect_id derived from work_item/operation/semantic payload generation

idempotency_and_concurrency_controls.repository_rule: Create immutable/new facts with create-if-absent where possible. Updates require current blob/head compare-and-swap. On conflict, refetch source/epoch/authority, revalidate ownership and only then retry; never blind-overwrite.
idempotency_and_concurrency_controls.scope_rule: Validate allowed write scope at dispatch and again before every material write. A stable scope hash lets the executor detect a worker whose intended permissions changed mid-run.
idempotency_and_concurrency_controls.side_effect_rule: Exactly-once transport is not assumed. For external effects use intent -> provider call with idempotency key when supported -> durable receipt -> reconciliation. If the provider lacks idempotency, isolate/serialize that effect and reconcile before retrying.
idempotency_and_concurrency_controls.aggregate_rule: No shared mutable counters for queued/running/done. Derive them from independent source objects so retries and concurrent workers cannot corrupt totals.
idempotency_and_concurrency_controls.collision_rule: One writer per canonical artifact. Intentional parallel alternatives must write isolated candidate namespaces/branches and converge later through one explicit steward/merger.
idempotency_and_concurrency_controls.late_worker_rule: A superseded/zombie worker's generation token or lease_epoch must fail authorization for canonical writes even if its process remains alive.

transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.failure: Launch request lost before backend acceptance
transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.observable: dispatch intent exists, no backend acceptance and no run artifact

transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.failure: Acceptance succeeds but ACK is lost
transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.observable: caller sees timeout/unknown outcome; run artifact may appear
transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.recovery: reconcile durable run first; retry same dispatch_id only if still absent
idempotent admission/claim returns existing logical launch rather than new work

transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.failure: Worker process starts but cannot create STARTED artifact
transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.observable: backend may show process, repository has no run proof
transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.recovery: worker must not perform material side effects; terminate/retry after reconciliation

transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.failure: STARTED durable, then worker crashes or loses progress channel
transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.recovery: SUSPECT -> reconcile -> revoke lease -> superseding run if policy allows
generation/lease guard denies canonical writes; retain isolated diagnostics only

transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.failure: RETURN commit succeeds but callback/notification is lost
transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.observable: durable RETURN exists while parent did not receive transport event
transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.recovery: scanner/compiler converges from repository truth; no execution retry

transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.failure: Notification claims completion before durable RETURN commit
transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.observable: callback says done but no RETURN exists
transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.recovery: treat as not durably returned; reconcile until RETURN or timeout boundary

transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.failure: Repository/API write times out with unknown commit outcome
transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.observable: client cannot tell whether write landed
transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.recovery: read target path/head before retrying; CAS/idempotency prevents duplicate semantic write

transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.failure: Public runtime/EPOCH publication lags source main
transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.recovery: surface PUBLISH_LAG; source-capable writer revalidates actual source head and collision scope instead of treating lag as worker failure

transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.observable: ready work remains queued; no run artifact
transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.recovery: bounded queue/backoff or alternate authorized adapter; never infer a permanent global platform limit from one backend

transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.observable: competing successor claims for same supersession generation
transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.recovery: CAS/unique generation claim admits one owner; loser reconciles to winner

transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.failure: Cancellation races with external side effect
transport_and_delivery_failure_modes.recovery: reconcile effect receipt first; cancellation is idempotent and prevents further unreceipted effects

tests_that_would_falsify_the_design: MISSED_SUBMIT: drop a launch before acceptance; detector must surface REQUESTED_NO_ARTIFACT and a retry must create exactly one run.
LOST_ACK: let STARTED commit succeed but drop launch ACK; retrying the same dispatch_id must observe/reuse the run, not create a duplicate.
DUPLICATE_DELIVERY: deliver the same dispatch twice concurrently; exactly one execution lease may own the logical attempt.
CAPACITY_BOUND: with capacity N and N+K ready jobs, no more than N leases may be live while K remain durably/derivably queued; changing N must not require schema changes.
CRASH_AFTER_STARTED: kill a worker after STARTED and before RETURN; it must become suspect/stale and be safely supersedable without blocking unrelated jobs.
ZOMBIE_WRITE: revive the old worker after successor ownership; every canonical/shared write from the old generation must be rejected.
RETURN_CALLBACK_LOSS: persist RETURN but drop notification; parent/compiler must still converge to RETURN_AVAILABLE and must not retry execution.
UNKNOWN_WRITE_OUTCOME: inject repository timeout after server-side commit; reconciliation must detect the existing write and avoid a duplicate semantic effect.
TWO_RETRY_RACE: start two coordinators after the same stale run; one successor lease wins deterministically and the other converges without dual writers.
CAS_CONFLICT: mutate a target between worker read/write; worker must refetch/revalidate rather than overwrite the newer value.
SIDE_EFFECT_REPLAY: crash after provider accepted an external effect but before local receipt write; retry/reconciliation must not repeat the effect when provider idempotency/receipt evidence exists.
SUPERSESSION_COUNTING: old + successor runs must count as one logical Work Item outcome and the superseded run must not retain a live collision.
EPOCH_LAG: make gh-pages EPOCH one commit behind main; write-capable execution should diagnose publication lag, revalidate source head, and continue only if its owned scope is still collision-free.
SCOPE_BREACH: worker attempts a path outside JOB write_scope; executor/write guard must reject it even if Git credentials technically permit the write.
CANCEL_RACE: cancel while work is active; repeated cancel requests are harmless and no new side effect may occur after cancellation ownership is durable.

TRANSPORT_OUTAGE: primary dispatch adapter is unavailable; system either uses an explicitly authorized alternate or reaches a bounded durable boundary without claiming Prometeo has a permanent concurrency limit.

evidence.supports: Prepared JOB before worker, independent worker run state, STARTED before material execution, RETURN before DONE, parent-derived aggregate state, no human result bus and no global locks/heartbeats by default.
Target execution plane requires bounded compute allocation, queue/cancellation/status, missed-job detection, idempotent retries and provenance.
Canonical delegated flow is prepared Work Item -> independent run -> durable RETURN -> parent integration/recovery.
Existing worker lifecycle, run metadata, RETURN states and supersession vocabulary to extend rather than replace.
Real missed-launch incident where dispatch was attempted but no repository-visible run/RETURN existed; artifact proof must outrank dispatch language.
Do not turn observed transport/backend failures or historical worker counts into hard platform limitations; retain retry/backoff and multi-session recovery.
Preserve source-of-truth rebuild, bounded retries/backoff, degraded/repairing modes and avoidance of split-brain authority.
Durable object graph, exactly-once intent for side effects, queues/retries/logs and a 0->M worker target decoupled from chat transport.
Current derived Agent Network already favors independent source objects and derived convergence rather than central mutable coordination.
Current regressions already exercise stale telemetry clamping, disjoint parallelism and derived runtime behavior; generic worker lease/missed-launch cases are the next missing falsification layer.
Concrete canary lifecycle and a recovered/retried repository update conflict demonstrate why execution state and write reconciliation must be durable and idempotent.
Adjacent Agent Network vNext scout independently recommends lifecycle normalization, missing-run detection, supersession lineage and publication-lag diagnostics as derived coordination features.
Public EPOCH projected main 5d95acece957 while source main was 068ae116..., a one-commit non-overlapping publication window that validates explicit PUBLISH_LAG handling.

tests.note: This work item is a read-only architecture scout; no runtime implementation or executable test files were authorized by its write scope.

unresolved: Numeric heartbeat/lease/deadline defaults must be measured per execution backend with canaries; inventing one universal timeout here would violate the anti-limitation rule.

The canonical durable home for dispatch intents/lease claims is not yet selected. It should be chosen so it remains independent-per-attempt or transactional rather than becoming one central mutable scheduler document.
Exactly-once external effects depend on provider idempotency/receipt capabilities. Providers without them require effect-specific serialization/reconciliation policy.
A promoted implementation needs a canonical execution-generation/dispatch-id format and explicit adapter contract for chat, GitHub/CI, cloud runners and future local/private executors.
WORKER_RUN_CONTRACT_V1 enumerates RETURNED/INTEGRATED while current delegated-control practice also uses DONE. vNext normalization should formally reconcile that vocabulary before implementation.
Lease enforcement must happen at the actual write/effect boundary; metadata-only supersession is insufficient against a live zombie worker.
